doc.title: Billy Taylor — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: How he fared as a high school student
summary: He was a fair student distracted by music and wide reading, including mythology from the Library of Congress, and barely passed math and Spanish.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Were you also a good student in the other subjects in high school?
Fair. When I applied myself I did well but I was so… I realize now that I was so enamored with music and I was so wrapped up in all kinds of music that… and

I read a lot in those days. So not only did I practice but I was reading novels. I found out in those days that the Library of Congress was my library so I could go to the library and get these wonderful books, fantasy books, all kinds of stuff. I was into reading things about… what would you call it, mythology. They myths of who are the gods of Norway and Sweden, and who are the… how did they relate to the Greek myths and so forth. That was fascinating to me because my mother had brought me up on fairy tales and so I read a lot of fairy tales and then I graduated to this mythology and stuff like that. So I had a lot of distractions, and so when it came to learning mathematics and Spanish… I must have taken Spanish for three years and man I barely scraped through, I could barely get through those courses and it wasn’t… wonderful teachers but I just wasn’t applying myself.
